root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every prime p > 3, define I: {1,...,p-1} -> {1,...,p-1} by I(k) being the unique integer with k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p). Let S = { k ∈ {1,...,p-2} : I(k+1) < I(k) }. Then |S| > p/4 - 1. Equivalently (since |S| is integral), |S| ≥ floor(p/4).

For all k in {1,...,p-1}, there exists a unique I(k) in {1,...,p-1} with k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p) (uniqueness follows from p prime and gcd(k,p)=1)
Define S = { k in {1,...,p-2} : I(k+1) < I(k) }
Claim: |S| > p/4 - 1 (equivalently, |S| ≥ floor(p/4) since |S| is an integer)

payload.theorem_nl: Let $p$ be a prime number greater than $3$. For each $k \\in \\{1,\\dots,p-1\\}$, let $I(k) \\in \\{1,2,\\dots,p-1\\}$ be such that $k \\cdot I(k) \\equiv 1 \\pmod{p}$. Prove that the number of integers $k \\in \\{1,\\dots,p-2\\}$ such that $I(k+1) < I(k)$ is greater than $p/4-1$.

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Fix a prime p>3 and write N(p) for the number of descents in the inverse sequence k -> I(k). First, L1 gives the inverse map as a well-defined permutation of {1,...,p-1}. By L2, counting descents is equivalent to counting indices k for which the pair (I(k),I(k+1)) lies in the strict lower triangle T_p of the square [1,p-1]^2. Next, L5 gives a disjoint union U of axis-parallel rectangles contained in T_p that misses only O(p) lattice points of T_p; L3 computes the triangle size exactly. Then apply the rectangle discrepancy estimate L4 to each rectangle in U and sum. The packaged consequence is L6, namely N(p) >= (p-2)/2 - C' sqrt(p) log(p)^2 for some absolute constant C'. Since sqrt(p) log(p)^2 = o(p), L7 yields a threshold P_0 beyond which this lower bound is stronger than p/4 - 1. Finally, L8 covers the finitely many primes below P_0 by direct verification. Combining the large-prime and small-prime cases yields the required inequality for every prime p>3.

steps.derives: For a fixed prime p>3, the inverse map I:{1,...,p-1}->{1,...,p-1} is well-defined, takes values in {1,...,p-1}, and all expressions I(k), I(k+1) with 1<=k<=p-2 are meaningful.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the existence-and-uniqueness conclusion of L1 specialized to the fixed prime p.

steps.derives: There exist pairwise disjoint axis-parallel rectangles R_1,...,R_m contained in T_p such that the union U=R_1∪...∪R_m satisfies |U| >= (p-1)(p-2)/2 - 2p.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L5 to obtain the rectangular inner approximation U of T_p. L3 supplies the exact size of T_p, so the lower bound can be read as losing at most 2p points from the triangle.

steps.derives: For each rectangle R_i in the family from A3, the count M_i := #{k in {1,...,p-2} : (I(k),I(k+1)) in R_i} satisfies M_i >= |R_i|/p - C*sqrt(p)*log(p)^2, where C is the absolute constant from L4.
steps.trivial_justification: This is the lower side of the two-sided discrepancy estimate from L4 applied separately to each rectangle R_i.

steps.derives: There exists an absolute constant C'>0 such that N(p) >= (p-2)/2 - C'*sqrt(p)*log(p)^2 for every prime p>3.
steps.trivial_justification: Because the rectangles from A3 are pairwise disjoint and all lie inside T_p, summing the bounds from A4 gives a lower bound for the number of k whose pair (I(k),I(k+1)) lies in U, hence also for the number lying in T_p. Using A2 converts that count into N(p). Lemma L6 packages exactly this summation-and-absorption argument, producing the stated global lower bound with a new absolute constant C'.

steps.derives: There exists an integer threshold P_0>=5 such that for every prime p>=P_0 one has N(p) > p/4 - 1.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L7 to the constant C' obtained in A5. Since N(p) satisfies the hypothesis of L7, the desired inequality follows for all sufficiently large primes.

steps.derives: For every prime p with 5<=p<P_0 one has N(p) > p/4 - 1.
steps.trivial_justification: L8 states that the finitely many small primes below the threshold can be checked directly.

steps.derives: For every prime p>3, if I(k) is the unique integer in {1,...,p-1} with k*I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p), then the number of integers k in {1,...,p-2} such that I(k+1) < I(k) is greater than p/4 - 1.
steps.trivial_justification: Every prime p>3 satisfies p>=5, so either p>=P_0 and A6 applies, or 5<=p<P_0 and A7 applies. In both cases the same conclusion holds. This is exactly the root theorem statement.

domain_restrictions: p is prime, so every k in {1,...,p-1} is invertible modulo p
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: The modular inverse map on the nonzero residue classes modulo p is a well-defined involutive permutation of {1,...,p-1}.
quantifier_order: There exists a unique I(k) in {1,...,p-1} with k*I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p)
witness_dependencies: I(k) depends only on p and k

lemmas.statement_nl: Let p be a prime number with p>3. For each integer k with 1<=k<=p-1, there exists a unique integer I(k) in {1,2,...,p-1} such that k*I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p). Moreover the map I:{1,2,...,p-1}->{1,2,...,p-1} is a permutation and satisfies I(I(k))=k for every k in {1,2,...,p-1}.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Recasts the theorem as a counting problem for visits of the sequence k -> (I(k),I(k+1)) to a triangular region.
lemmas.self_check_notes: Immediate unpacking of the definition of T_p and N(p).

domain_restrictions: I(k) and I(k+1) both lie in {1,...,p-1}
quantifier_order: Define I and N(p) as stated
witness_dependencies: The pair (I(k),I(k+1)) depends on p and k

lemmas.statement_nl: Let p be a prime number with p>3, let I:{1,2,...,p-1}->{1,2,...,p-1} be defined by k*I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p), and define N(p)=|{k in {1,2,...,p-2}: I(k+1)<I(k)}|. Also define the strict lower triangle T_p={(x,y) in Z^2 : 1<=x<=p-1, 1<=y<=p-1, y<x}. Then N(p) is exactly the number of integers k in {1,2,...,p-2} for which the pair (I(k),I(k+1)) lies in T_p.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Supplies the main-term area/count for the target region inside the square.
lemmas.self_check_notes: Sum over x: for each x there are x-1 admissible values of y.

domain_restrictions: x and y are integers in [1,p-1]

lemmas.statement_nl: Let p be an integer with p>=5, and let T_p={(x,y) in Z^2 : 1<=x<=p-1, 1<=y<=p-1, y<x}. Then the number of lattice points in T_p is exactly (p-1)(p-2)/2.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: This is the analytic input: the consecutive inverse pairs are equidistributed in axis-parallel rectangles up to square-root error.
lemmas.self_check_notes: This is a standard consequence of exponential-sum bounds for the affine curve x*y ≡ 1 and (x+1)z ≡ 1 modulo p, combined with completion of sums. It is much stronger than the target inequality but is a known type of estimate.

domain_restrictions: R is axis-parallel and contained in the integer square [1,p-1]^2
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Uniform rectangle discrepancy bound: #{k in {1,...,p-2} : (I(k),I(k+1)) in R} = |R|/p + O(sqrt(p) log(p)^2), with an absolute implied constant.
quantifier_order: There exists an absolute constant C>0
For all integer rectangles R=[a,b]∩Z × [c,d]∩Z inside [1,p-1]^2

lemmas.statement_nl: There exists an absolute constant C>0 such that the following holds. Let p be a prime number with p>3, let I:{1,2,...,p-1}->{1,2,...,p-1} be defined by k*I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p), and let R be any axis-parallel rectangle of the form R=[a,b]∩Z × [c,d]∩Z with 1<=a<=b<=p-1 and 1<=c<=d<=p-1. Then the number of integers k in {1,2,...,p-2} for which (I(k),I(k+1)) lies in R differs from |R|/p by at most C*sqrt(p)*log(p)^2.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Allows the triangle-counting problem to be reduced to finitely many rectangle counts, where the discrepancy estimate from L4 applies directly.
lemmas.self_check_notes: A staircase decomposition of the triangle gives such an approximation; losing O(p) points is elementary.

domain_restrictions: Each R_i is axis-parallel, consists of integer lattice points, and lies inside T_p
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: There is a disjoint rectangular inner approximation of T_p whose missed set has size at most 2p.
quantifier_order: There exists a finite family of pairwise disjoint rectangles R_1,...,R_m

lemmas.statement_nl: Let p be an integer with p>=5, and let T_p={(x,y) in Z^2 : 1<=x<=p-1, 1<=y<=p-1, y<x}. There exists a family of pairwise disjoint axis-parallel rectangles R_1,...,R_m contained in T_p such that |R_1 ∪ ... ∪ R_m| >= (p-1)(p-2)/2 - 2p. Equivalently, the strict lower triangle T_p can be approximated from inside by a disjoint union of axis-parallel rectangles while losing at most 2p lattice points.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Combines the geometric triangle approximation with rectangle equidistribution to extract a usable lower bound for the descent count.
lemmas.self_check_notes: Apply the discrepancy estimate to each disjoint rectangle from the inner approximation and sum the errors; the main term is the total area divided by p, which is ((p-1)(p-2)/2 - O(p))/p = (p-2)/2 - O(1). This O(1) term is absorbed into O(sqrt(p) log^2 p).

domain_restrictions: N(p) counts k in {1,...,p-2} with I(k+1)<I(k)
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Uniform rectangle discrepancy implies the asymptotic lower bound N(p) >= (p-2)/2 - O(sqrt(p) log(p)^2).

Then there exists an absolute constant C'>0

lemmas.statement_nl: Assume there exists an absolute constant C>0 with the rectangle discrepancy property stated as follows: for every prime p>3, every inverse map I(k) modulo p, and every axis-parallel rectangle R inside [1,p-1]^2, one has | #{k in {1,...,p-2} : (I(k),I(k+1)) in R} - |R|/p | <= C*sqrt(p)*log(p)^2. Then there exists an absolute constant C'>0 such that for every prime p>3, if N(p)=|{k in {1,...,p-2}: I(k+1)<I(k)}|, then N(p) >= (p-2)/2 - C'*sqrt(p)*log(p)^2.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Turns the asymptotic estimate from L6 into the explicit target inequality for all sufficiently large primes.
lemmas.self_check_notes: Elementary comparison of growth rates: sqrt(x) log(x)^2 = o(x).

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: The term x/4 dominates C' sqrt(x) log(x)^2 for all sufficiently large x, so the asymptotic lower bound implies the desired inequality for all sufficiently large primes.

lemmas.statement_nl: Let C'>0 be a fixed real constant. There exists an integer P_0>=5 such that for every real number x>=P_0 one has (x-2)/2 - C'*sqrt(x)*log(x)^2 > x/4 - 1. In particular, if p is a prime with p>=P_0 and a quantity N(p) satisfies N(p) >= (p-2)/2 - C'*sqrt(p)*log(p)^2, then N(p) > p/4 - 1.

lemmas.role_in_assembly: Handles the finite exceptional range below the asymptotic threshold P_0.

lemmas.statement_nl: For every prime p with 5<=p<P_0, where P_0 is any fixed integer, let I_p(k) be the inverse of k modulo p in {1,...,p-1} and let N(p)=|{k in {1,...,p-2}: I_p(k+1)<I_p(k)}|. Then the statement N(p) > p/4 - 1 can be verified by a finite case check over the finitely many primes p in the interval [5,P_0).

candidates.strategy_summary: Use a distribution-theoretic approach: encode the descent condition I(k+1)<I(k) as the event that the consecutive inverse pair (I(k), I(k+1)) lies in the strict lower triangle of the square [1,p-1]^2. Invoke a standard equidistribution estimate for the affine curve k -> (I(k), I(k+1)) modulo p, approximate the triangle from inside by a union of axis-parallel rectangles, obtain an asymptotic lower bound N(p) >= (p-2)/2 - O(sqrt(p) log^2 p), and then finish by a finite verification for the remaining small primes.
